Фея Драже съ принцемъ Коклюшемъ стоятъ въ сахарномъ кіоскѣ, украшенномъ дельфинами, изъ пастей которыхъ бьютъ фонтаны смородиннаго сиропа, оршада, лимонада и другихъ прохладительныхъ и сладкихъ напитковъ. Ожида пріѣзда Кляры съ принцемъ Щелкунчикомъ и приготовивъ имъ встрѣчу, фея Драже вмѣстѣ съ принцемъ Коклюшемъ выходять изъ кіоска; феи—мелодій, цвѣтовъ, картинокъ, фруктъ, куколъ, ночей, плясуновъ и сновидѣній и конфекты — карамель, ячменный сахаръ, шоколадъ, petits-fours, нуга, мятныя лепешки, драже, фисташки и macarons, живописно группируясь, преклоняются передъ ней, а серебряные солдатики отдаютъ ей честь. Мажордомъ, увидѣвъ приближеніе ожидаемыхъ гостей, разставляетъ маленькихъ мавровъ и пажей, у которыхъ головы изъ жемчужинъ, туловище изъ рубиновъ и изумрудовъ, а ноги изъ чистаго золота; въ рукахъ они держать горящіе факелы. По рѣкѣ тихо подплываетъ Клара и Щелкунчикъ въ вызолоченной орѣховой скорлупѣ. При выходѣ ихъ на берегъ, серебряные
review_1892-93_SP_ballet_p012__b003.en: Scene 3 (Act 2). The scene depicts the Palace of Delights—Confitureburg. Fairy Dragée stands with Prince Coculus in a sugar kiosk adorned with dolphins, from whose mouths spurt fountains of currant syrup, orgeat, lemonade, and other cooling and sweet beverages. Having awaited Clara’s arrival with Prince Nutcracker and prepared a welcome for them, Fairy Dragée, together with Prince Coculus, steps out of the kiosk; the fairies—of Melodies, Flowers, Pictures, Fruits, Dolls, Nights, Dancers, and Dreams—and the confections—caramel, barley sugar, chocolate, petits-fours, nougat, mint cakes, dragées, pistachios, and macarons—group themselves picturesquely and bow before her, while the silver soldiers render her a salute. The major-domo, spotting the approach of the expected guests, stations small Moors and pages whose heads are made of pearls, torsos of rubies and emeralds, and legs of pure gold; they hold burning torches in their hands. review_1892-93_SP_ballet_p010__b001.ru: какъ должно съ нимъ обращаться. Фрицъ отнимаетъ игрушку у Клары и заставляетъ Щелкунчика разгрызать самые болѣшіе орѣхи, отчего у того ломается челюсть. Клара поднимаетъ брошенного Шелкунчика, объязываетъ ему голову, убаюкиваетъ, танцуя съ нимъ «polca berceuse», и укладываетъ на кровать своей любимой куклы. По приглашенію Зильбергауса всѣ гости, болѣшіе и малые, танцуютъ старинный танецъ «grossfater», по окончаніи котораго г-жа Зильбергаусъ напоминаетъ мужу, что уже поздно и дѣтямъ пора ложиться спать. Клара хочетъ взять Щелкунчика съ собой, но отецъ ей въ этомъ отказываетъ. Дѣтей уводятъ, гости прощаются съ хозяевами и постепенно расходятся. Залъ нѣкоторое время остается пустымъ. Безпокоясь о больномъ Щелкунчикѣ, Клара, какъ только утихло все въ домѣ, рѣшается навѣстить его и входитъ въ темный залъ. Шорохъ, бѣготня и царапанье мышей подъ поломъ приковываютъ Клару на мѣстѣ. Изъ щелей подъ карнизами видно множество блестящихъ огоньковъ, комната наполняется мышами и испуганная Клара бѣжитъ къ кроваткѣ больного Шелкунчика, ища тамъ защиты. Луна, свѣтитъ въ окно; ѣлка постепенно ростетъ и достигаетъ огромныхъ размѣровъ; куклы и игрушки оживаютъ: зайчики бьютъ тревогу, часовой у будки салютуетъ ружьемъ и стрѣляетъ, куколки бѣгаютъ въ испугѣ, размахивая руками, ища гдѣ бы укрыться; появляется отрядъ пряничныхъ солдатъ и строится въ ряды. Непріятельское мышиное войско начинаетъ наступленіе, оттѣсняетъ пряничныхъ солдатъ и, одержавъ полную побѣду, возвращается съ добычей—кусками пряниковъ, которые и пожираетъ тутъ же. Щелкунчикъ, видя неудачу пряничнаго войска, быстро вскакиваетъ съ постели и приказываетъ зайчикамъ немедленно снова бить тревогу. Крышки слетаютъ съ коробокъ, въ которыхъ лежали оловянные солдатики, и изъ нихъ поспѣшно вылѣзаютъ стрѣлки, гренадеры, гусары и артиллеристы съ мѣдными пушками. Мышиный царь приказываетъ своему войску возобновить нападеніе. Мыши нѣсколько разъ атакуютъ непріятеля, но съ большимъ урономъ отступаютъ назадъ; тогда мышиный царь вступаетъ въ единоборство съ Щелкунчикомъ. Клара, видя опасность, грозящую ея любимцу, снимаетъ съ ноги башмачекъ и изо всѣхъ силъ бросаетъ его въ царя мышей; Щелкунчикъ ранитъ своего врага, который вмѣстѣ со своими подданными спасается бѣгствомъ. Щелкунчикъ, превратившись въ красиваго принца, становится на колѣни передъ Кларой и проситъ ее слѣдовать за собою. Они идутъ къ елкѣ и скрываются въ ея вѣтвяхъ. Картина 2 я. review_1892-93_SP_ballet_p010__b001.en: how one should behave with him. Fritz snatches the toy from Clara and forces the Nutcracker to crack the largest nuts, causing his jaw to break. Clara picks up the discarded Nutcracker, bandages his head, lulls him to sleep by dancing with him a “polca berceuse,” and lays him on the bed of her favorite doll. At Silberhaus’s invitation, all the guests—both adults and children—dance the old-fashioned “grossfater” dance; upon its conclusion, Mme Silberhaus reminds her husband that it is already late and that the children ought to go to bed. Clara wishes to take the Nutcracker with her, but her father refuses her request. The children are led away; the guests bid farewell to their hosts and gradually disperse. The hall remains empty for some time. Worried about the ailing Nutcracker, Clara, as soon as the house grows quiet, resolves to visit him and enters the dark hall. The rustling, scurrying, and scratching of mice beneath the floor hold Clara motionless in place. From cracks beneath the cornices, countless gleaming lights appear; the room fills with mice, and frightened Clara flees to the sick Nutcracker’s little bed, seeking refuge there. Moonlight shines through the window; the Christmas tree gradually grows and attains enormous size; dolls and toys come to life: rabbits sound the alarm, the sentry at his booth salutes with his rifle and fires, dolls run about in terror, waving their arms and searching for places to hide; a troop of gingerbread soldiers appears and forms ranks. The hostile mouse army begins its advance, drives back the gingerbread soldiers, and, having achieved a complete victory, returns with its spoils—pieces of gingerbread—which it devours on the spot. Seeing the gingerbread army’s defeat, the Nutcracker quickly leaps from his bed and commands the rabbits to sound the alarm once more without delay. Lids fly off the boxes in which the tin soldiers had lain, and marksmen, grenadiers, hussars, and artillerymen with copper cannons hastily emerge from them. The Mouse King orders his troops to renew their attack. The mice launch several assaults upon the enemy but retreat backward with heavy losses; then the Mouse King engages the Nutcracker in single combat. Clara, seeing the danger threatening her beloved, removes a slipper from her foot and hurls it with all her strength at the Mouse King; the Nutcracker wounds his foe, who flees together with his subjects. The Nutcracker, transformed into a handsome prince, kneels before Clara and begs her to follow him. They walk toward the Christmas tree and vanish among its branches. Scene 2. review_1903-04_SP_ballet_p006__b003.ru: Новый балетъ г. Перро отличается тѣми же качествами, какъ и всѣ предыдущія его хореографическія созданія. Въ немъ то же изящество, то же богатство фантазіи, перевитой съ картинами житейскаго быта, та же полнота и прелесть колорита, та же грація въ выполненіи. И здѣсь, какъ въ другихъ его балетахъ, танцы перестаютъ быть простой безпредметной пляской, а получаютъ мимическій смыслъ и соединяютъ въ себѣ выраженіе чувства съ граціей движеній. Поэтическій сюжетъ балета для живописца-балетмейстера представилъ обширное поле для самыхъ обворожительныхъ картинъ. Перро показалъ себя тутъ великимъ художникомъ. Сценическое па съ весломъ въ первомъ дѣйствіи, между Наядой и тремя рыбаками—верхъ пластической прелести! Каждая группа этого танца— новая картина, которая такъ и просится на полотно. Баркаролла, танцуемая самимъ Перро и г-жею Андреяновой, полна жизни, одушевленія и граціи. Сцена съ букетомъ, во второмъ дѣйствіи, между К. Гризи и Перро, самый роскошный отрывокъ изъ буколической поэзіи древнихъ. Наконецъ, сцена—танецъ между Наядой, рыбакомъ и г-жею Андреяновой, въ третьемъ дѣйствіи, такая прелестная смѣсь мимики, граціи, чувства и нѣги, что отъ нея трудно отвести глаза. Кромѣ этого стройность группировки и красота положеній кордебалетныхъ танцевъ дѣлаютъ этотъ балетъ еще очаровательнѣе. Появленіе рыбака съ мандолиной на колодцѣ и поѣздъ молодыхъ въ неаполитанской каріолѣ, запряженной волами и украшенной гирляндами, живо напоминаютъ двѣ картины Леопольда
review_1903-04_SP_ballet_p006__b003.en: The new ballet by Mr. Perrot possesses the same qualities as all his previous choreographic creations. It displays the same elegance, the same wealth of fantasy interwoven with scenes from everyday life, the same fullness and charm of coloration, the same grace in execution. Here, as in his other ballets, dancing ceases to be mere aimless frolic and acquires mimetic meaning, uniting expression of feeling with the grace of movement. The poetic subject of the ballet offered the painter-choreographer an extensive field for the most enchanting tableaux. Perrot revealed himself here as a great artist. The scenic pas with oars in the first act, between the Naiad and three fishermen, is the pinnacle of plastic charm! Each group in this dance constitutes a new picture, one that seems expressly designed for transfer onto canvas. The barcarolle, danced by Perrot himself and Mme Andreyanova, is full of life, animation, and grace. The scene with the bouquet in the second act, between K. Grisi and Perrot, is the most sumptuous excerpt from ancient bucolic poetry. Finally, the dance-scene in the third act between the Naiad, the fisherman, and Mme Andreyanova is such a delightful blend of mime, grace, feeling, and languor that it is difficult to tear one’s eyes away from it. In addition, the precision of grouping and the beauty of poses in the corps de ballet dances render this ballet even more captivating. The fisherman’s appearance with a mandolin on the well, and the procession of youths in a Neapolitan carriola drawn by oxen and adorned with garlands, vividly recall two paintings by Leopold.

review_1903-04_SP_ballet_p007__b001.ru: Робера—„Сицилійскій Импровизаторъ“ и „Возвращеніе съ жатвы“, находящіяся въ Луврскомъ музеймъ. Если можно упрекнуть новый балетъ за чтонибудь, это за его названіе.—„Наяда“. Дѣйствіе видимо происходитъ между италіанскими рыбаками въ послѣднія времена среднихъ вѣковъ; у италіанцевъ не могло существовать понятія о наядахъ, полубогиняхъ древнихъ грековъ. Всѣ европейскіе народы первыхъ эпохъ христіанства были заражены элементарнымъ суевѣріемъ, но они признавали стихійныя существа, какъ отдѣльныя силы природы, а не какъ божества. Понятія ихъ, соотвѣтствующія древней идѣѣ о наядахъ, населяли рѣки и моря ундинами, никсами неками и морскими людьми. Эти понятія германскихъ народовъ гораздо отвлеченнеѣ и заключаютъ въ себѣ болѣе поэзіи, чѣмъ положительныя идеи древней міѳологіи. Ундины, русалки, олицетворяя въ себѣ непоборимыя силы водной стихіи, дѣйствуютъ самобытно, между тѣмъ какъ древнія нимфы вода не что иное, какъ низшіе разряды божествъ, исполняющіе только волю высшихъ: это подданные царства Нептуна и Амфитриты. Объ исполненіи этого балета довольно сказать, что въ немъ участвовали Перро, г-жи Андреянова и Карлотта Гризи, чтобы дать понятіе, что онъ былъ исполненъ превосходно. Г-жа Андреянова маленькой своей роли Джіатины умѣла придать жизнь и значеніе, и сцены ея съ Матео (Перро) въ хижинѣ, и съ Наядой—рыбакомъ, въ третьемъ дѣйствіи, принадлежатъ къ прелестнѣйшимъ мимическихъ исполненіямъ. О Перро нечего и говорить: мима, выше его, въ настоящее время мы не знаемъ, Карлотта Гризи превзошла самое себя въ роли Наяды. Здѣсь ея легкость, увлекательное порханіе, наивная кокетливость были какъ нельзя болѣе у мѣста. Прекрасно исполняла также г-жа Никитина повелительницу Наядъ и г. Фредеракъ—Антоніо. Очаровательными Наядами были: г-жа Прихунова, Амосова 1-я, Соколова, Снѣткова 1-я и Макарова. Танцы въ балетѣ исполняли: въ 1-й картинѣ: г-жа Карлотта Гризи, г-жи Амосова 1-я, Соколова, гг. review_1903-04_SP_ballet_p007__b001.en: Robert—“The Sicilian Improviser” and “The Return from the Harvest,” housed in the Louvre Museum. If one may reproach the new ballet for anything, it is for its title—“Naiad.” The action evidently takes place among Italian fishermen in the late Middle Ages; the Italians could not have held any conception of naiads—the semi-divine nymphs of ancient Greek mythology. All European peoples of the early Christian era were imbued with elementary superstition, yet they recognized elemental beings as distinct natural forces, not as deities. Their notions corresponding to the ancient idea of naiads populated rivers and seas with undines, nixies, necks, and sea-men. These Germanic conceptions are far more abstract and contain greater poetic resonance than the concrete ideas of ancient mythology. Undines and rusalki, personifying the irresistible forces of the watery element, act autonomously, whereas the ancient water-nymphs are nothing more than lower ranks of divinities, executing solely the will of higher powers: they are subjects of Neptune’s and Amphitrite’s realm. Regarding the performance of this ballet, it suffices to state that Perrot, Mmes Andreyanova and Carlotta Grisi took part in it, to convey that it was superbly executed. Mme Andreyanova, in her small role of Giacinta, succeeded in endowing it with life and significance; her scenes with Matteo (Perrot) in the hut, and with the Naiad-fisherman in the third act, belong among the most delightful mimetic performances. As for Perrot, there is nothing to say: there exists no mime superior to him at present; Carlotta Grisi surpassed even herself in the role of the Naiad—here her lightness, captivating fluttering, and naive coquettishness were perfectly suited to the part. Mme Nikitina also performed splendidly as the Queen of the Naiads, and Mr. Frederak as Antonio. Enchanting Naiads included Mmes Prikhunova, Amosova 1st, Sokolova, Snetkova 1st, and Makarova. review_1901-02_SP_ballet_p008__b002.en: On 21 November, a benefit performance was held for A. F. Beketi at the Mariinsky Theatre in honour of his twenty-five years of service; “Paquita”, a ballet in three acts by Foucher and Mazilier, music by Deldevez, with some numbers by Minkus, staged by Ballet Master M. I. Petipa, was presented for the seventeenth time since its revival. The roles were performed as follows: Paquita (for the first time) — Mme Zambelli; Count d’Erville — Mr Gerdt. At the conclusion of the performance, a divertissement was given featuring artists from the Imperial Moscow Theatres, Mme Geltsier and Mr Tikhomirov, and Mme Preobrazhenskaya, Petipa 1st, Messrs Gerdt and Beketi. review_1892-93_SP_ballet_p004__b003.ru: Роль Пахиты исполнялась г-жею Андреяновою, танцовавшею, между прочимъ, съ Петипа-сыномъ, нынѣшнимъ главнымъ балетмейстеромъ (дебютировавшимъ въ «Пахитѣ»), вальсъ «Pas de folie», имѣвшее большой успѣхъ, равно, какъ и особенно понравившіеся публикѣ «Pas de trois» и «Pas de manteaux», исполненные первыми сюжетами тогдашней труппы: г. Іогансономъ и г-жами Смирновой, Яковлевой, Никитиной, Прихуновой, Соколовой, Пановой и др. Это «Pas de manteaux» сохранено въ балетѣ «Пахита» и до настоящаго времени, не смотря на то, что многіе номера танцевъ измѣнены при послѣдующихъ его возобновленіяхъ.
review_1892-93_SP_ballet_p004__b003.en: The role of Paquita was performed by Mme Andreyanova, who danced, among other things, the waltz “Pas de folie” with Petipa’s son, the present chief ballet master (who had made his debut in “Paquita”), a number that met with great success, as did the “Pas de trois” and “Pas de manteaux,” which were especially well received by the public and performed by the leading dancers of the company at that time: Mr. Johanson and Mmes Smirnova, Yakovleva, Nikitina, Prikhunova, Sokolova, Panova, and others. This “Pas de manteaux” has been retained in the ballet “Paquita” to the present day, despite the fact that many dance numbers were altered in subsequent revivals of the work.

И. Петипа «Grand pas», исполнявшимся балериною, 6-ю солистками и 8-ю вторыми танцовщицами. Музыка для этихъ номеровъ была сочинена г. Л. Минкусомъ.

I. Petipa 1st, performed by the ballerina, six soloists, and eight second dancers. Music for these numbers was composed by Mr. L. Minkus.

review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p013__b003.en: On 16 February, at the Mariinsky Theatre, to close the ballet performances before Great Lent, the following were presented: Act III of the ballet “Paquita” by Foucher and Mazilier; the comic ballet “The Magic Flute” in one act; and, for the first time, the ballet “The Fairy of the Dolls”, in one act and two scenes. The scenario of the ballet “The Fairy of the Dolls” was by MM. Asreytera and Gaul. The dances and scenes were composed and staged by MM. N. Legat and S. Legat. Music by Mr. Bauer.

review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p013__b002.en: The ballet’s synopsis and illustrations will appear in Volume XV of the Yearbook, in the report on the activities of the Moscow Ballet Troupe during the 1904–05 season.

review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p013__b004.ru: Хозяинъ игрушечнаго магазина сидитъ у конторки и повѣряетъ счета. Приказчики его въ это время приводятъ въ порядокъ шкапъ, на полкахъ котораго разставлены механическія куклы. Въ магазинъ входитъ почтальонъ и сдаетъ хозяину нѣсколько пакетовъ и заказныхъ писемъ подъ росписку. Затѣмъ появляется разсылный, съ большимъ коробомъ въ рукахъ, который онъ вручаетъ главному приказчику. Хозяинъ велитъ дать посыльному на чай, что тотъ и исполняетъ. По разсылный, взглянувъ на врученную ему монету, находитъ, что его недостаточно вознаградили, и требуетъ прибавки. Послѣ нѣкоторыхъ пререканій, дѣло улаживается къ обоюдному удовольствію, и хозяинъ магазина, по уходѣ разсылнаго, вскрываетъ полученные письма и посылки. Какъ разъ въ это время
review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p013__b004.en: The owner of the toy shop sits at the counter and checks his accounts. His clerks, meanwhile, tidy up the cabinet whose shelves are lined with mechanical dolls. A postman enters the shop and hands the owner several packages and registered letters, receiving his signature in return. Then a delivery boy appears, holding a large box in his hands, which he hands over to the head clerk. The shop owner orders that the delivery boy be given a tip, which is duly carried out. However, glancing at the coin handed to him, the delivery boy considers his reward insufficient and demands an increase. After some argument, the matter is settled to the mutual satisfaction of both parties, and the shop owner, after the delivery boy has departed, opens the letters and packages he has received. review_1905-06_SP_ballet_p009__b002.ru: 12-го февраля, для закрытія балетныхъ спектаклей передъ Великимъ постомъ, состоялся бенефисъ солиста Его Величества П. А. Гердтъ за XLVлѣтнюю службу. Павелъ Александровичъ Гердтъ хореографическій талантъ обнаружилъ, когда онъ, будучи еще ребенкомъ, выступилъ въ 1858 г. въ бенефисъ балерины г-жи Фридбергъ. М. И. Петипа, бывшій въ то время преподавателемъ танцевъ, предсказалъ ему блестящее будущее и принялъ его въ свой классъ. Окончивъ С.-Петербургское Театральное училище въ 1865 г., пройдя курсъ танцевъ подъ руководствомъ Петипа - отца, Пименова, Іогансона, М. И. Петипа и др. П. А. уже съ первыхъ лѣтъ своей служебной дѣятельности: пользовался большими симпатіями публики. Первый бенефисъ, полученный Гердтомъ—31 января 1871 г. совмѣстно съ г-жами Вяземъ и Вергиной. Первый самостоятельный бенефисъ за 10-ти лѣтнюю службу онъ получилъ 12 января 1875 г., поставивъ въ этотъ день балетъ „Голубая георгина“. П. А. пользовался одинаковымъ успѣхомъ какъ въ танцахъ, такъ и въ мимико-драматическихъ роляхъ. За 40лѣтнюю службу на СПБ. сценѣ, выступавшій въ десяткахъ балетовъ, въ которыхъ онъ исполнялъ главныя мимическія роли, онъ навсегда останется въ памяти балетомановъ.
review_1905-06_SP_ballet_p009__b002.en: On 12 February, a benefit performance was held for His Majesty’s soloist P. A. Gerdt to close the ballet season before Great Lent, honouring his forty-fifth year of service. Pavel Aleksandrovich Gerdt revealed his choreographic talent while still a child, when he appeared in 1858 in the benefit performance of the ballerina Mme Fridberg. M. I. Petipa, who at that time was a dance instructor, predicted for him a brilliant future and admitted him into his class. Having graduated from the St. Petersburg Theatre School in 1865, having completed his dance studies under the guidance of Petipa the elder, Pimenov, Johansson, M. I. Petipa, and others, P. A. enjoyed great public favour from the very first years of his professional career. His first benefit, shared with Mmes Vyazem and Vergina, took place on 31 January 1871. His first independent benefit, awarded after ten years of service, occurred on 12 January 1875, when he staged the ballet “The Blue Dahlia” on that day. P. A. enjoyed equal success both in dancing and in mimico-dramatic roles. Having performed over forty years on the St. Petersburg stage in dozens of ballets, in which he danced leading mimetic roles, he will remain forever in the memory of ballet enthusiasts.

Онъ входитъ, прекланяется передъ свѣтскимъ повелителемъ и заявляетъ, что имѣетъ сообщить ему великую тайну. Всѣ удаляются, кромѣ дочери раджи, которая прячется за занавѣсомъ. Но расчетъ брамина не оправды-
review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p014__b004.en: At this moment, the arrival of the Great Brahmin is announced. He enters, bows before the secular ruler, and declares that he has a great secret to impart to him. All withdraw except the rajah’s daughter, who hides behind the curtain. The Great Brahmin has come with the aim of avenging himself upon Solor for his audacious love for the chosen one of his heart. He informs the rajah of the young kshatriya’s love for Nikiya, calculating that the ruler’s wrath will descend upon Solor for having dared to slight his daughter, that he will destroy his rival, and thus aid him in gaining possession of the lovely Nikiya. But the Brahmin’s calculation does not pan out—

review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p015__b002.ru: вается: упрямый раджа остается при своемъ намѣреніи выдать свою дочь Гамзатти за Солора, а жертвою должна пасть Никія. Это рѣшеніе приводитъ въ ужасъ влюбленнаго брамина. Онъ авторитетно заявляетъ раджѣ, что такая расправа надъ жрицею храма неминуемо должна разгнѣвать Вишну, но раджа настаиваетъ на своемъ и объявляетъ ему, что завтра на праздникъ Бадрината, когда Никія будетъ танцовать, въ ея корзину съ цвѣтами положать змѣю. Вполнѣ удовлетворенный придуманнымъ наказаніемъ, Дугманта уходитъ съ опечаленнымъ браминомъ.
review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p015__b002.en: It is decided: the stubborn rajah remains firm in his intention to marry off his daughter Gamzatti to Solor, while Nikiya must be the victim. This decision horrifies the lovestruck Brahmin. He authoritatively informs the rajah that such punishment of a temple priestess will inevitably enrage Vishnu; yet the rajah insists on his plan and declares to him that tomorrow, during the festival of Badrinath—when Nikiya will be dancing—a snake will be placed in her flower basket. Fully satisfied with this devised punishment, Dugmanta departs with the sorrowful Brahmin.

review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p012__b004.ru: Солоръ осторожно приближается къ пагодѣ, стучитъ, три раза, на этотъ сигналъ окно отворяется и, съ помощью факира, Никія спускается въ рощу. Молодые люди признаются въ обоюдной любви и Никія соглашается бѣжать изъ храма, но беретъ съ Солора клятву, что онъ никогда не полюбитъ другой. Солоръ клянется Брамою и Вишну, что до конца жизни останется ей вѣренъ. Между тѣмъ, наступаетъ уже и утро. Факиръ докладываетъ, что охотники вернулись съ преслѣдованія тигра. Одновременно съ этимъ растворяется дверь пагоды и баядерки выходятъ, направляясь къ пруду, за водою. Никія, никѣмъ не замѣченная, быстро удаляется въ пагоду, а Солоръ прячется за деревья. Обмѣнявшись послѣднимъ взглядомъ съ Никіей, столщей опять у своего окна, Солоръ удаляется со своими охотниками, едва удостоивъ вниманія принесенную добычу—великолѣпнаго ти-
review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p012__b004.en: Solor cautiously approaches the pagoda, knocks three times; at this signal the window opens, and Nikiya descends into the grove with the fakir’s help. The young people confess their mutual love, and Nikiya agrees to flee the temple but extracts from Solor a vow that he will never love another woman. Solor swears by Brahma and Vishnu that he will remain faithful to her for the rest of his life. Meanwhile, dawn is already breaking. The fakir reports that the hunters have returned from their pursuit of the tiger. Simultaneously, the pagoda door opens, and the bayaderes emerge, heading toward the pond for water. Unnoticed by anyone, Nikiya quickly retreats into the pagoda, while Solor hides behind the trees. Exchanging a final glance with Nikiya, who once again stands at her window, Solor departs with his hunters, barely deigning to notice the captured prey—a magnificent tiger.

review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p013__b002.en: The second act takes place in the palace of the all-powerful Rajah of Golconda, Dugmanta. The rajah plays chess with one of his kshatriyas, while bayaderes perform various dances. Upon completion of the game, Dugmanta sends for his daughter Gamzatti.

review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p013__b004.ru: Слѣдуя обычаю, онъ обручилъ эту дочь еще въ дѣтствѣ. Теперь настало время торжественно закрѣпить этотъ бракъ и онъ объявляетъ это Гамзатти. Зовутъ и жениха. Оказывается, что это Солоръ. Грозный раджа объявляетъ и ему свое намѣреніе отпраздновать свадьбу и съ гордостью снимаетъ съ головы дочери вуаль, увѣренный, что поразитъ жениха необычайной красотой невѣсты. Солоръ, дѣйствительно, отдаетъ ей справедливость—онъ пораженъ красотою ея. Но эта красота все-таки не въ силахъ заглушить въ немъ пламенной любви его къ Никіи и онъ грустно опускаетъ свой взоръ.
review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p013__b004.en: Following custom, he had betrothed this daughter while she was still a child. Now the time has come to solemnly confirm this marriage, and he announces it to Gamzatti. The bridegroom is summoned—and it turns out to be Solor. The stern rajah declares his intention to celebrate the wedding and proudly lifts the veil from his daughter’s head, confident that the bridegroom will be struck by the extraordinary beauty of his fiancée. Solor indeed does her justice—he is struck by her beauty. Yet this beauty is still powerless to quell the ardent love he bears for Nikiya, and he sadly lowers his gaze.

review_1906-07_SP_ballet_p003__b002.ru: 5-го ноября была представлена, въ 17-й разъ по возобновленіи, «Баядерка», балетъ М. Петипа, музыка Минкуса, при участіи въ немъ г-жи Павловой 2-й (Никея); г-жи Сѣдовой (Гамзатти); г. Гердта, солиста Его Величества (Солора). Въ 3-й картинѣ Ману исполняли г-жа Трефилова и воспитанницы Императорскаго театральнаго училища.
review_1906-07_SP_ballet_p003__b002.en: On 5 November, “La Bayadère,” a ballet by M. Petipa to music by Minkus, was presented for the 17th time since its revival, with the participation of Mme Pavlova 2nd (Nikia); Mme Sedova (Gamzatti); and Mr Gerdt, soloist of His Majesty (Solor). In the 3rd tableau, the role of Manu was performed by Mme Trefilova and students of the Imperial Theatre School.

review_1906-07_SP_ballet_p003__b003.ru: 10 декабря состоялся бенефисъ кордебалетныхъ артистовъ и артистокъ; данъ былъ въ первый разъ: «Котъ въ сапогахъ», балетъ въ 2-хъ дѣйствіяхъ (3-хъ картинахъ). Постановка и танцы балетмейстера Н. Г. Легатъ. Сюжетъ заимствованъ изъ сказки Перро. Музыка А. Н. Михайлова. Новыя декораціи г. Ламбина. Исполняли роли: принцессы Клементины—г-жа Трефилова; короля Хризостома—г. Гердтъ, солистъ Его Величества; Клотильды и Гертруды, подругъ принцессы—г-жи Кякштъ и Карсавина; придворныхъ дамъ—г-жи Рыхлякова 1-я, Ваганова, Егорова, Преображенская и Вилль; маркиза Карабасъ, сына мельника — гг. Легатъ и Обуховъ; Кота въ сапогахъ—г. Стуколкинъ; приближенныхъ короля—гг. Больмъ и Андріановъ; Сагадоры, чародѣя—г. Солянниковъ; невольницы Фатьмы—г-жа Чумакова.
review_1906-07_SP_ballet_p003__b003.en: On 10 December, a benefit performance was held for the corps de ballet artists and ballerinas; the ballet “Puss in Boots,” in two acts (three scenes), was staged for the first time. Staging and choreography by Ballet Master N. G. Legat. The plot is drawn from Perrault’s fairy tale. Music by A. N. Mikhailov. New scenery by Mr. Lambin. Roles were performed as follows: Princess Clémentine—Mme Trefilova; King Chrysostom—Mr. Gerdt, Soloist of His Majesty; Clotilde and Gertrude, the princess’s maids of honour—Mmes Kyakshet and Karsavina; Court Ladies—Mmes Rukhlyakova 1st, Vaganova, Egorova, Preobrazhenskaya, and Ville; Marquis de Carabas, the miller’s son—MM. Legat and Obukhov; Puss in Boots—Mr. Stukolkin; the King’s courtiers—MM. Bolm and Adrianov; Sagador, the sorcerer—Mr. Solyannikov; Fatima, the slave girl—Mme Chumakova.

review_1903-04_MSK_ballet_p023__b019.ru: Танецъ маріонетокъ (муз. Лядова)—г-жа Домашева, гг. Бекъ и Рябцевъ. Исполняли соло: на скрипкѣ— г. Крейнъ; на віолончели—г. Аспергеръ; на арфѣ—г. Омэ. Оркестромъ дирижировалъ г. Арендсъ.
review_1903-04_MSK_ballet_p023__b019.en: Marionette Dance (music by Lyadov)—Mme Domasheva, MM. Bek and Ryabtsev. Solo performances were given on violin by Mr. Krein; on cello by Mr. Asperger; on harp by Mr. Ome. The orchestra was conducted by Mr. Arend.

review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p015__b004.ru: Никія робко, съ поклонами, приближается къ дочери раджи. Та объявляетъ ей о предстоящей свадьбѣ и приглашаетъ ее танцовать на празднествѣ. Никія, конечно, польщена такой честью. Тогда Гамзатти показываетъ ей портретъ Солора и требуетъ, чтобы баядерка отказалась отъ своего возлюбленнаго. Никія приходитъ въ негодованіе отъ такого требованія и заявляетъ, что скорѣе умретъ, чѣмъ откажется отъ своей любви. Отъ угрозъ Гамзатти переходитъ къ попыткѣ соблазнить Никію подарками, а затѣмъ рѣшается даже и просить ее. Но и мольбы ничего не помогаютъ. Скромная баядерка входитъ въ ярость, схватываетъ кинжалъ и бросается на Гамзатти, но невольница обезоруживаетъ ее. Никія убѣгаетъ, а оскорбленная Гамзатти подымается и обрекаетъ ее на смерть, отъ которой могла бы спасти. Приговоръ надъ Никіей предполагается исполнить во время празднества. При поднятіи занавѣса, въ 5-й картинѣ, мы видимъ процессію, въ которой участвуютъ брамины, баядерки разныхъ разрядовъ,
review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p015__b004.en: Nikiya timidly approaches the rajah’s daughter with bows. The latter informs her of the upcoming wedding and invites her to dance at the celebration. Nikiya, of course, is flattered by such an honor. Then Gamzatti shows her Solor’s portrait and demands that the bayadère renounce her beloved. Nikiya is outraged by this demand and declares she would rather die than forsake her love. Gamzatti shifts from threats to attempting to seduce Nikiya with gifts, and then even resorts to pleading with her. But entreaties prove futile. The modest bayadère flies into a rage, seizes a dagger, and rushes at Gamzatti; however, the slave disarms her. Nikiya flees, while the humiliated Gamzatti rises and condemns her to death—a fate from which she might have been saved. The sentence upon Nikiya is scheduled for execution during the celebration. At the rise of the curtain in Scene 5, we see a procession in which brahmins and bayadères of various ranks take part.

review_1910-11_SP_ballet_p003__b002.ru: ковъ; нѣкоторыя роли изъ ея репертуара были переданы г-жѣ Карсавиной, и можно прямо сказать, что, за вычетомъ гастролей г-жи Преображенской и послѣдовавшихъ за ними такихъ же выступленій г-жи Кшесинской, весь остальной сезонъ г-жа Карсавина вынесла на своихъ плечахъ. Индивидуальныя особенности ея таланта помогли ей съ полнымъ достоинствомъ выступать даже въ балетахъ, неразрывно связанныхъ съ именемъ г-жи Павловой. Первой серьезной работой явилась роль Никіи въ «Баядеркѣ», шедшей вторымъ спектаклямъ сезона, 5-го сентября, а самой значительной по своимъ художественнымъ результатамъ вышла «Жизель», которую г-жа Карсавина танцовала впервые въ отчетномъ сезонѣ 21-го ноября. Здѣсь талантливая артистка обнаружила въ 1-мъ актѣ драматическую игру, а во второмъ ея танцы отличались замѣчательной воздушностью, отчетливостью техническаго рисунка и поэзіей. Съ большимъ успѣхомъ танцовала она также въ «Эвникѣ», гдѣ отведено много мѣста чистой мимодрамѣ.
review_1910-11_SP_ballet_p003__b002.en: Kov; some roles from her repertoire were transferred to Mme Karsavina, and it can be stated outright that, discounting Mme Preobrazhenskaya’s guest appearances and the subsequent guest appearances by Mme Kshesinskaya, Mme Karsavina carried the entire remainder of the season on her shoulders. The individual qualities of her talent enabled her to perform with full dignity even in ballets inextricably linked to Mme Pavlova’s name. Her first serious role was Nikiya in La Bayadère, staged as the second performance of the season on 5 September; her most artistically significant achievement proved to be Giselle, which Mme Karsavina danced for the first time during the reporting season on 21 November. Here the talented artist displayed dramatic acting in Act I, while her dancing in Act II was distinguished by remarkable lightness, clarity of technical execution, and poetry. She also danced with great success in Evnika, a ballet offering ample scope for pure mimodrama.

review_1910-11_SP_ballet_p003__b003.ru: 24-го октября впервые въ сезонѣ былъ данъ спектакль, составленный изъ трехъ балетовъ постановки г. Фокина: «Египетскія ночи», «Шопеніана» и «Эвника». Какъ разъ передъ этимъ произошло назначеніе г. Фокина балетмейстеромъ Императорскихъ театровъ, что явилось въ жизни нашего балета крайне важнымъ событіемъ. Балетное искусство у насъ, какъ и вездѣ въ Европѣ, даже въ центрахъ наивысшаго процвѣтанія, въ Парижѣ и Миланѣ, средоточіяхъ двухъ школъ классическаго танца, французской и итальянской, дошло до такой точки, когда уже невозможна стала его жизнь въ прежнихъ формахъ, сдѣлавшихся бездушными, сухими, скучными. Академизмъ классическихъ пріемовъ началъ превращаться въ гимнастику, въ акробатизмъ, но это уже нисколько не искусство, еще меньше танецъ, какъ выраженіе сложныхъ душевныхъ переживаній въ ритмѣ живого и прекраснаго человѣческаго тѣла. Явилась Айседора Дёнканъ и приподняла завѣсу надъ грядущимъ балетнаго искусства. А что сдѣлалъ г. Фокинъ? Онъ пошелъ по ея стопамъ. Это тѣмъ болѣе представляется смѣлымъ, что, рѣшаясь на подобный шагъ, г. Фокинъ долженъ былъ порвать со всѣмъ наслѣдіемъ своихъ предшественниковъ въ дѣлѣ постановки балетовъ,
review_1910-11_SP_ballet_p003__b003.en: On 24 October, for the first time this season, a performance was given comprising three ballets choreographed by Mr. Fokine: “Egyptian Nights,” “Chopiniana,” and “Eunika.” Just prior to this, Mr. Fokine had been appointed Ballet Master of the Imperial Theatres—an event of exceptional importance in the history of our ballet. Ballet art among us, as everywhere in Europe—even in the very centers of its highest flourishing, Paris and Milan, the seats of the two classical dance schools, the French and the Italian—had reached such a point that its existence in former forms had become impossible; those forms had grown soulless, dry, and dull. Academicism in classical technique had begun to degenerate into gymnastics, into acrobatics—but this is no longer art at all, and even less so dance, understood as the expression of complex inner experiences through the rhythm of a living, beautiful human body. Isadora Duncan appeared and lifted the veil over ballet art’s future. And what did Mr. Fokine do? He followed in her footsteps. This appears all the bolder in that, resolving upon such a step, Mr. Fokine had to break entirely with the entire legacy of his predecessors in ballet production.

review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p010__b005.ru: нея свою страсть и, забывъ всякую осторожность, подходитъ къ ней. review_1900-01_SP_ballet_p010__b005.en: He confesses his passion to her and, forgetting all caution, approaches her. Forgetting his spiritual office, bound by a vow of celibacy, he declares his love to her, offers her his protection, and promises to make her supreme in this temple and compel the people to worship her as a deity.

review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p001__b006.ru: 25-го сентября данъ былъ въ 11-й разъ балетъ «Баядерка», въ 4-хъ дѣйствіяхъ, соч. М. Петипа, музыка Минкуса, съ г-жою Павловой 2 въ роли Никіи и г. Гердтомъ въ роли Солора.
review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p001__b006.en: On 25 September, the ballet “La Bayadère,” in four acts, choreographed by M. Petipa, music by Minkus, was performed for the 11th time, with Mme Pavlova 2nd as Nikiya and Mr Gerdt as Solor.

review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p001__b005.ru: 22-го сентября на сценѣ Маріинскаго театра были даны: въ 6-й разъ «Арлекинада», балетъ въ 2-хъ дѣйствіяхъ, соч. М. Петипа, муз. Р. review_1902-03_SP_ballet_p001__b005.en: On 22 September, the following were performed on the stage of the Mariinsky Theatre: “Harlequinade”, a ballet in two acts, choreographed by M. Petipa, music by R. Drigo, for the sixth time, with Mme Preobrazhenskaya in the role of Columbine and the rest of the cast unchanged (only Mr Aistov in the role of Leander was replaced by Mr Voronkov); and “Grazziella”, a ballet in one act, choreographed by Saint-Léon, music by Pugni, staged by L. Ivanov, with Mme Trefilova in the role of Grazziella and Mr S. Legat in the role of Genariello; in the latter ballet, a new pas de deux (music by Chopin, orchestrated by Mr A. Glazunov) was inserted, performed by Mlle Pavlova 2nd and Mr Bekefi.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p005__b001.en: of Rov (Act II, Scenes 1 and 2 of Act III, Act IV, and the apotheosis) and artist I. P. Andreev (Act I and Scene 3 of Act III).

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p005__b003.ru: «Литовскій танецъ» Г-жа Гельцеръ и г. Лукьяновъ

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b003.ru: Апоѳеозъ. Славянскій Олимпъ. Млада вводитъ Яромира въ царство боговъ.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b003.en: Apoteosis. The Slavic Olympus. Mlada introduces Yaromir into the realm of the gods.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b002.ru: Дѣйствіе IV. Храмъ Радегаста въ Ретрѣ. Бракъ Яромира съ Войславой. Появленіе Млады. Яромиръ отказывается отъ брака съ Войславой. Мщеніе Морены. Разрушеніе храма и наводненіе.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b002.en: Act IV. The Temple of Radegast in Rethra. The marriage of Yaromir and Voislava. The appearance of Mlada. Yaromir refuses to marry Voislava. Morana’s vengeance. The destruction of the temple and the flood.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b004.ru: Первая постановка балета «Млада» состоялась въ С.-Петербургѣ, въ Большомъ театрѣ, 2-го декабря 1879 года, въ бенефисъ балерины г-жи Евгеніи Соколовой. Первый составъ исполнителей былъ слѣдующій: г. Кшесинскій (Мстивой), г-жа Горшенкова (Войслава), г. Гердтъ (Яромиръ), г-жа Евг. Соколова (тѣнь Млады), г-жа Савицкая (Святохна), г-жа Жебелева (мамка), г. Карсавинъ (шутъ), г. Н. Богдановъ (оруженосецъ), г. Пишо (старый копьеносецъ), г-жа Симская 1-я (Морена) и др. Кромѣ перечисленныхъ артистовъ, въ танцахъ участвовали: г-жи Радина, Никитина, Жукова 1-я, Шапошникова, Амосова, Петипа, Іогансонъ, Фролова, Петрова, Воронова, Симская 2-я, Глаголева, Крюгеръ 2-я, Ѳедорова 2-я, Лезенская, Александрова, Жукова 2-я, Тистрова, Предтечина и др., гг. Л. Ивановъ, Гельцеръ Леоновъ, Татариновъ, Стуколкинъ 2-й и др. Декораціи были написаны: профессоромъ Шишковымъ, академикомъ Бочаровымъ и художниками Вагнеромъ, Егоровымъ и Лупановымъ.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b004.en: The first production of the ballet “Mlada” took place in St. Petersburg at the Bolshoi Theatre on 2 December 1879, as a benefit performance for the ballerina Mme Evgeniya Sokolova. The original cast was as follows: Mr Kshesinsky (Mstivoy), Mme Gorshenkova (Voislava), Mr Gerdt (Yaromir), Mme Evgeniya Sokolova (the Shade of Mlada), Mme Savitskaya (Svyatokhna), Mme Zhebeleva (the Nurse), Mr Karsavin (the Jester), Mr N. Bogdanov (the Squire), Mr Pisho (the Elder Spear-Bearer), Mme Simskaya 1st (Moréna), and others. In addition to the artists listed above, the following participated in the dances: Mmes Radina, Nikitina, Zhukova 1st, Shaposhnikova, Amosova, Petipa, Ioganson, Frolova, Petrova, Voronova, Simskaya 2nd, Glagoleva, Kryuger 2nd, Fedorova 2nd, Lezenskaya, Aleksandrova, Zhukova 2nd, Tistrova, Predtechina, and others; MM. L. Ivanov, Gel’tser, Leonov, Tatarinov, Stukolkin 2nd, and others. The scenery was painted by Professor Shishkov, Academician Bocharov, and the artists Wagner, Egorov, and Lupanov.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b005.ru: Г. Лукьяновъ—въ роли старого копьеносца («Млада», балетъ М. И. Петипа).
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b005.en: Mr. Lukyanov—in the role of the old spear-bearer (“Mlada,” ballet by M. I. Petipa).

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b006.ru: При нынѣшнемъ возобновленіи балета «Млада» новыхъ декорацій написано не было, а воспользовались тѣми, которыя были изготовлены въ 1892 году для оперы того же названія, сочиненной Н. А. Римскимъ-Корсаковымъ по той же программѣ. Рисунки всѣхъ этихъ декорацій были уже помѣщены въ «Ежегодникѣ Императорскихъ театровъ» (см. сезонъ 1892—1893 гг., стр. 167—182); онѣ принадлежатъ кисти нынѣ уже умершихъ академика М. И. Боча-
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p004__b006.en: For the current revival of the ballet “Mlada,” no new scenery was painted; instead, the scenery created in 1892 for the opera of the same name—composed by N. A. Rimsky-Korsakov to the same libretto—was reused. Drawings of all these sets had already been published in the Yearbook of the Imperial Theatres (see the 1892–1893 season, pp. 167–182); they are the work of the late Academician M. I. Bocharov.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p003__b005.ru: Въ краткихъ словахъ вотъ программа этого балета.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p003__b005.en: In brief, here is the program of this ballet.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p003__b007.ru: Дѣйствіе I. Дворецъ князя Мстивоя, въ городѣ Ретрѣ, близъ Лабы. Пріѣздъ князя Яромира. Княжна Войслава для обольщенія Яромира призываетъ подземную богиню Морену. Приготовленіе къ празднику Купала. Лада усыпляетъ Яромира. Первый сонъ: Объясненіе въ любви Яромира и Млады. Второй сонъ: Бракъ Яромира съ Младою въ храмѣ Свѣтовита, въ Арконѣ, и затѣмъ отравленіе Млады Мстивоемъ и Войславою.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p003__b007.en: Act I. Prince Mstivoy’s palace in the city of Rethra, near the Elbe River. Prince Yaromir’s arrival. Princess Voislava invokes the chthonic goddess Morena to seduce Yaromir. Preparations for the Kupala festival. Lada puts Yaromir to sleep. First dream: Yaromir’s declaration of love to Mlada. Second dream: Yaromir’s marriage to Mlada in the temple of Svetovit in Arkona, followed by Mlada’s poisoning by Mstivoy and Voislava.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p003__b006.ru: Дѣйствіе происходитъ въ IX—X вѣкѣ, въ славянскихъ земляхъ Балтійскаго поморья.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p003__b006.en: The action takes place in the 9th–10th centuries, in the Slavic lands of the Baltic coast.

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p005__b005.ru: Въ 1-мъ дѣйствіи: Дыню рядовую — г-жи Петипа 1-я, Петипа 2-я (Леонова 1-я), гг. Гердтъ, Облаковъ 1-й и воспитанницы и воспитанники Императорскаго С.-Петербургскаго театральнаго училища. Плясковицу — г-жа Оголейтъ 1-я и г. Лукьяновъ. Пляску шута—г. Ширяевъ(г. Сергѣевъ).
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p005__b005.en: In Act I: The Row of Melons—Mmes Petipa 1st, Petipa 2nd (Leonova 1st), MM. Gerdt, Oblakov 1st, and students of the Imperial St. Petersburg Theatre School. The Dance of the Melons—Mme Ogoleyt 1st and Mr. Lukyanov. The Jester’s Dance—Mr. Shiryayev (Mr. Sergeyev).

review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p008__b001.ru: Въ 4-мъ дѣйствіи: Танецъ съ тѣнью—г-жа Кшесинская 2-я и г. Гердтъ.
review_1896-97_SP_ballet_p008__b001.en: In Act IV: Shadow Dance—Mme Kshesinskaya 2nd and Mr Gerdt.

review_1907-08_SP_ballet_p014__b007.ru: Всѣхъ балетныхъ спектаклей въ сезонѣ 1907 и 1908 г. было дано 52, въ которые вошли 22 балета. Изъ нихъ 18 капитальныхъ и 4 второстепенныхъ, считая тутъ и три, вновь поставленные балета. Одинъ изъ нихъ въ 5-ти дѣйствіяхъ и 8-ми картинахъ, П. А. Маржецкаго, музыка Ѳ. А. Гартмана «Аленькій цвѣточекъ» выдержалъ шесть представленій, шесть разъ также давали балетъ въ 3-хъ картинкахъ «Павильонъ Армиды», А. Бенуа, музыка Н. Черепнина и одинъ разъ былъ поставленъ новый балетъ въ 1-мъ дѣйствіи В. В. Свѣтлова, музыка г. Давидова «Принцъ Садовникъ». По частной иниціативѣ г. Фокинымъ было поставлено нѣсколько красивыхъ номеровъ: «Лебедь», музыка Сенъ-Санса для г-жи Павловой 2-й, «Ассирійскій танецъ» для г-жи Карсавиной. Особенныхъ перемѣнъ въ личномъ составѣ не произошло. Покинули труппу за выслугой лѣтъ нѣсколько второстепенныхъ артистовъ. Бенефисовъ въ сезонѣ было два: кордебалета и М. М. Петипа,
review_1907-08_SP_ballet_p014__b007.en: A total of 52 ballet performances were given during the 1907–1908 season, comprising 22 ballets. Of these, 18 were major and 4 minor works, including three newly staged ballets. One of them, in five acts and eight tableaux, was P. A. Margetsky’s “The Little Red Flower,” with music by F. A. Hartmann; it ran for six performances. The ballet in three tableaux “The Pavilion of Armida” by A. Benois, with music by N. Tcherepnin, was also performed six times; and a new one-act ballet, “The Prince Gardener” by V. V. Svetlov, with music by Mr. Davidov, was staged once. On Mr. Fokine’s private initiative, several beautiful numbers were staged: “The Swan,” with music by Saint-Saëns, for Mme Pavlova 2nd, and “The Assyrian Dance” for Mme Karsavina. No significant changes occurred in the company’s personnel. Several minor artists retired from the troupe upon completion of their required years of service. There were two benefit performances during the season: one for the corps de ballet and one for MM. Petipa.

review_1905-06_SP_ballet_p010__b003.ru: 9-го апрѣля воспитанниками и воспитанницами Императорскаго Театральнаго Училища представленъ былъ: „Сонъ въ лѣтнюю ночь“ фантастическій балетъ въ 1-мъ дѣйствіи, соч. солиста Его Величества М. Петипа, музыка Мендельсона. Танцы и группы вновь поставлены г. Фокинымъ. Роли въ балетѣ распредѣлились такъ: Титанія—в-ца Кандина; Оберонъ—в-ца Николаидисъ; пажъ Титаніи—в-ца Кирхгеймъ; Робинъ— в-ца Лопухова; дровосѣкъ—в-къ Исаевъ; Эльфы (свита Титаніи и свита Оберона), бабочки, кузнечики, розы, летучія мыши и совы. Танцовали: Andante: бабочки—в-ца Смирнова и в-къ Нижинскій; розы—в-цы Чумакова и Пильцъ; в-ки: Эрлеръ и Бурманъ, в-цы: Мазырина, Леонтьева 1, Соболева, Георгіевская, Нижинская, Власова, Барановичъ 1, Барановичъ 2; Пуни, Декомбъ, Клемецкая, Подраменцова, Люкомъ и Добролюбова. Танецъ кузнечиковъ—в-ки Пономаревъ, Владиміровъ, Спѣсивцевъ, Ивановъ, Гуммертъ, Улановъ, Усачевъ и Герасимовъ. Полетъ бабочекъ (муз. Шопена) в-ца Смирнова и в-къ Нижинскій. review_1905-06_SP_ballet_p010__b003.en: On 9 April, a performance of “A Midsummer Night’s Dream”, a fantastic ballet in one act, composed by His Majesty’s soloist M. Petipa, with music by Mendelssohn, was presented by the students of the Imperial Theatre School. The dances and groupings were newly staged by Mr. Fokine. The roles in the ballet were distributed as follows: Titania—student Kandina; Oberon—student Nikolaïdis; Titania’s page—student Kirkhgeim; Robin—student Lopukhova; the woodcutter—student Isaev; Elves (Titania’s retinue and Oberon’s retinue), butterflies, grasshoppers, roses, bats, and owls. Danced: Andante: butterflies—student Smirnova and student Nijinsky; roses—students Chumakova and Pilts; students Erler and Burman; students Mazyrina, Leont’eva 1st, Soboleva, Georgievskaya, Nijinskaya, Vlasova, Baranovich 1st, Baranovich 2nd; Punin, Dekomb, Klemetskaya, Podramentsova, Lyukom, and Dobrolyubova. Grasshopper dance—students Ponomarev, Vladimirov, Spesivtsev, Ivanov, Gummet, Ulanov, Usachev, and Gerasimov. Flight of the butterflies (music by Chopin)—student Smirnova and student Nijinsky. Variations: 1) student Chumakova, 2) student Smirnova. Waltz fantasy (music by M. Glinka)—students Smirnova, Chumakova, Pilts, student Nijinsky, and others. Entrance of Titania—student Kandina. Scherzo—students Kandina, Nikolaïdis, Kirkhgeim, Lopukhova, Gerdt, Chernysheva, Pyuman, Shiryaeva, Karzhavina, Lyukom, Legat, Bibel, and El’man. Battle of the elves with bats and owls—students Gerdt, Chernysheva, Pyuman, and Shiryaeva; students Litavkin, Romanov 1st, Orlov, Oblakov, Prokhorov, Sergeev, Romanov 2nd, Fedorov, Khristapson, and Khrapis. review_1905-06_SP_ballet_p010__b002.ru: Офиціальный актъ юбилейнаго торжества состоялся послѣ первой картины, „Жавотты“: П. А. Гердта окружила вся балетная труппа при громѣ рукоплесканій, какъ его товарищей и товарокъ, такъ и всей публики. Г. Сергѣевъ, режиссеръ балетной труппы привѣтствовалъ юбиляра отъ имени его сослуживцевъ, которые поднесли ему цѣнный подарокъ. Затѣмъ шло привѣтствіе и вѣнокъ отъ русской драматической труппы; отъ имени французской труппы говорилъ г. Делормъ, а г-жа Дево поднесла лавровый вѣнокъ, и была прочитана поздравительная депеша отъ оперной труппы Маріинскаго театра.
review_1905-06_SP_ballet_p010__b002.en: The official ceremony of the jubilee celebration took place after the first tableau, “Javotte”: P. A. Gerdt was surrounded by the entire ballet company amid thunderous applause from both his colleagues and the audience. Mr. Sergeyev, ballet company director, addressed the jubilarian on behalf of his fellow dancers, who presented him with a valuable gift. Next followed greetings and a wreath from the Russian dramatic company; Mr. Delorm spoke on behalf of the French company, and Mme Devaux presented a laurel wreath; a congratulatory telegram from the Mariinsky Theatre’s opera company was also read aloud.

For the initial performances of this ballet, the corps de ballet consisted of students of the St. Petersburg Theatre School.

Спектакль этотъ состоялъ изъ отрывковъ произведеній покойнаго композитора, а именно сюда вошли: 1-е дѣйствіе оперы «Орлеанская дѣва»; арія изъ оперы «Опричникъ»; 2-я картина 1-го дѣйствія оперы «Пиковая дама»; «Коронаціонная кантата»; 2-е дѣйствіе балета «Лебединое озеро», музыка котораго написана П. review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p023__b003.en: On 17 February, a performance “in memory of P. I. Tchaikovsky” was given at the Mariinsky Theatre. This performance consisted of excerpts from the late composer’s works, specifically: Act I of the opera The Maid of Orleans; an aria from the opera The Oprichnik; Scene 2 of Act I of the opera The Queen of Spades; the Coronation Cantata; and Act II of the ballet Swan Lake, music for which was composed by P. I. Tchaikovsky.

review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p023__b004.ru: Балетъ «Лебединое озеро», соч. бывшаго балетмейстера Московскихъ театровъ—Рейзингера, на нашей сценѣ никогда не исполнялся, такъ что указанный отрывокъ явился новинкою для петербургской публики. «Лебединое озеро» было впервые дано въ Москвѣ, на сценѣ Большаго театра, 20-го февраля 1877 года, въ бенефисъ балерины г-жи Карпаковой, которая и исполнила въ немъ главную роль—Одетты.
review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p023__b004.en: The ballet “Swan Lake,” composed by the former ballet master of the Moscow Theatres—Reisinger—had never before been performed on our stage, so the excerpt indicated here was a novelty for the St. Petersburg public. “Swan Lake” was first given in Moscow, on the stage of the Bolshoi Theatre, on 20 February 1877, at the benefit performance of the ballerina Mme Karpakova, who performed the principal role of Odette.

Confident that Odile and Odette are one and the same person, he selects her as his bride (“Pas d’action”—Mme Len’yani; MM. Gerdt, Gorski, and Bulgakov). Von Rothbart solemnly takes his daughter’s hand and hands it over to the young man, who, before all present, pronounces his vow of eternal love. At this moment Siegfried sees Odette at the window; he realizes he has fallen victim to deception, but it is already too late—the vow has been spoken. Rothbart and Odile vanish. Now Odette must remain forever in the power of the evil genius, who appears in the guise of an owl.

Одетта, пользуясь, что она еще въ образѣ дѣвы, рѣшается скорѣе погибнуть въ волнахъ озера, чѣмъ жить безъ Зигфрида. Подруги напрасно пытаются утѣшить ее. Вбѣгаетъ Зигфридъ; онъ ищетъ Одетту, чтобы, упавъ къ ея ногамъ, вымолить прощеніе за невольную измѣну: онъ любитъ ее одну и произнесъ клятву вѣрности
review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p019__b006.en: Tsova, Troitskaya, Savitskaya, Kshesinskaya 1st, Ogoleyt 2nd, Vasilieva, Matveeva 3rd, Aistova, Tsalisson, Ryabova, Stepanova 3rd, Fonareva, Kasatkina, Borkhardt, Trefilova, Rikhlyakova 2nd, Ofitserova, Lavrentieva, and Kunitskaya). Odette rushes in. The swans joyfully greet her; but, learning of Siegfried’s betrayal, they fall into despair: all is lost—the evil genius has triumphed, and poor Odette has no salvation; she is condemned for eternity to be the slave of malevolent enchantments. Odette, taking advantage of the fact that she is still in the form of a maiden, resolves to perish more quickly in the lake’s waves than to live without Siegfried. Her companions vainly attempt to console her. Siegfried rushes in; he seeks Odette in order to fall at her feet and beg forgiveness for his involuntary betrayal: he loves only her and has sworn an oath of fidelity.

review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p013__b001.ru: столы и скрыть слѣды пиршества. Молодежь и Вольфгангъ дѣлаютъ усиліе, чтобы казаться трезвыми. Входитъ принцесса, предшествуемая свитой, — Зигфридъ идетъ на встрѣчу матери, почтительно ее привѣтствуя. Она ласково упрекаетъ его за то, что онъ пытается обмануть ее, — ей извѣстно, что онъ пировалъ сейчасъ, и пришла она не за тѣмъ, чтобы мѣшать ему веселиться въ кругу товарищей, а за тѣмъ, чтобы напомнить ему, что насталъ послѣдній день его холостой жизни и что завтра онъ долженъ сдѣлаться женихомъ. На вопросъ: кто его невѣста? — принцесса отвѣчаетъ, что это рѣшить завтрашній балъ, на который она созвала всѣхъ дѣвушекъ, достойныхъ стать ея дочерью и его женою; онъ выберетъ самъ наиболѣе ему нравящуюся. Разрѣшивъ продолжать прерванное пиршество, принцесса уходитъ. Принцъ задумчивъ: ему грустно разстаться съ привольной, холостой жизнью. Бенно уговариваетъ его не портить заботой о грядущемъ—приятнаго настоящаго. Зигфридъ подаетъ знакъ къ продолженію увеселеній; пиръ и танцы возобновляются. Совершенно опьянѣвшій Вольфгангъ смѣшитъ всѣхъ своимъ участіемъ въ танцахъ. Вечерѣтъ. Еще одинъ прощальный танецъ—и пора расходиться. Танецъ съ кубками («Danse au cliquetis de verres»—всѣ участвующіе). Пролетаетъ стая лебедей. Молодежи не до сна,—видъ лебедей наводитъ ихъ на мысль закончить этотъ день охотой. Бенно знаетъ, куда слетаются лебеди на ночь; оставивъ опьянѣвшаго Вольфганга, Зигфридъ и молодые люди уходятъ.
review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p013__b001.en: tables and conceal the traces of the feast. The young people and Wolfgang make an effort to appear sober. The Princess enters, preceded by her retinue; Siegfried goes to meet his mother and greets her respectfully. She affectionately reproaches him for trying to deceive her—she knows he has just been feasting, and she has come not to interfere with his merrymaking among friends, but to remind him that this is the last day of his bachelor life and that tomorrow he must become a bridegroom. To his question, “Who is my bride?” the Princess replies that this will be decided at tomorrow’s ball, to which she has summoned all maidens worthy of becoming her daughter-in-law and his wife; he himself will choose the one most pleasing to him. Permitting the interrupted feast to continue, the Princess departs. The Prince is pensive: he is saddened at the thought of parting with his carefree, bachelor life. Benno urges him not to spoil the pleasant present with worries about the future. Siegfried gives the signal to resume the festivities; the feast and dancing recommence. Thoroughly intoxicated, Wolfgang amuses everyone with his participation in the dancing. Evening approaches. One final farewell dance—and it is time to disperse. The Dance with Goblets (“Danse au cliquetis de verres”—all participants). A flock of swans flies past. The young people are not sleepy—the sight of the swans inspires them to conclude this day with a hunt. Benno knows where the swans gather at night; leaving the intoxicated Wolfgang behind, Siegfried and the young men depart.

review_1910-11_SP_ballet_p005__b002.ru: вслѣдствіе той точности, естественности, живости и пластичности каждаго движенія, которымъ могъ бы позавидовать любой танцовщикъ изъ молодыхъ. За 50 лѣтъ своей дѣятельности кому только изъ знаменитыхъ балеринъ русскихъ и иностранныхъ не служилъ Гердтъ надежнѣйшимъ кавалеромъ, пока онъ исполнялъ классическіе танцы; впослѣдствіи онъ перешелъ на танцы болѣе характерные и мимическія роли. Полувѣковой юбилей его службы искусству былъ отпразднованъ съ необычайной торжественностью; шелъ балетъ «Синяя борода», вновь поставленный балетмейстеромъ Легатъ; бенефиціантъ исполнялъ роль Синей бороды, а главную женскую роль Изоры—г-жа Кшесинская.

Лебеди, обратившись въ юныхъ красавицъ, окружаютъ Бенно, пораженнаго волшебнымъ явленьемъ и безсильного противъ ихъ чаръ. Его товарищи возвращаются; при ихъ появлении, лебеди отступаютъ. Молодые люди собираются стрѣлять въ нихъ. Входитъ принцъ и тоже прицѣливается... Но въ это время развалины освѣщаются волшебнымъ свѣтомъ, и появляется Одетта, умоляющая о пощадѣ. review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p014__b001.en: directing his companions to report to the Prince that they have found a flock, remains alone. The swans, transformed into young beauties, surround Benno, who is struck by the magical apparition and powerless against their enchantments. His companions return; at their appearance, the swans retreat. The young men gather to shoot at them. The Prince enters and likewise takes aim… But at that moment the ruins are illuminated by magical light, and Odette appears, imploring mercy. Siegfried, struck by her beauty, forbids his companions to shoot (“Scène dansante”—Mme Léonide and Mr Gerdt). She expresses her gratitude to him and relates that she, Princess Odette, and the maidens subject to her, are unhappy victims of a malevolent spirit who has bewitched them: they are condemned to assume the form of swans by day and may retain their human shape only by night near these ruins.

review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p016__b002.en: Act II. A hall. Everything is prepared for the celebration. The master of ceremonies gives the servants final instructions; he greets and seats the arriving guests. Entrance of the Princess and Siegfried. Procession of the brides and their parents. (“Valse des fiancées”—Mmes Ivanova, Leonova, Petipa 2nd, Noskova, Lits, Kuskova, and Mr Gerdt). The Princess-Mother asks her son which of the girls pleases him most. Siegfried finds them all charming, yet sees none to whom he could swear eternal love. Trumpets announce the arrival of new guests. Von Rothbart enters with his daughter Odile. Siegfried is struck by her resemblance to Odette and enthusiastically greets her. Odette, in the form of a swan, appears at the window, warning her beloved against the sorcerer’s enchantments; but the Prince, captivated by the beauty of the new guest, hears and sees nothing but her. Dancing resumes (“Danse Espagnole”—Mmes Skorsyuk, Obukhova, Messrs Shiryaev and Litavkin. “Danse Venitienne”—Mmes Savitskaya, Isaeva 1st, Kunitskaya, Lavrentyeva, Rikhartova, Ryabova, Dorina, Levina, Matveyeva 3rd, Pavlova, Matveyeva 1st, Stepanova 2nd, Tselikhova, Radina, Aistova, Konetskaya, Messrs Ivanov, Mar—

review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p016__b001.ru: и освободить Одетту. Послѣдняя отвѣчаетъ, что это невозможно: погибель злаго генія наступитъ только въ тотъ мигъ, когда какой-нибудь безумецъ принесетъ себя въ жертву любви къ Одеттѣ. Зигфридъ готовъ и на это,—ради нея ему погибнуть отрадно. Одетта вѣритъ его любви, вѣритъ, что она — первая его любовь. Но завтра наступитъ день, когда ко двору его матери явится цѣлый сонмъ красавицъ, и онъ будетъ обязанъ избрать одну изъ нихъ себѣ въ супруги. Зигфридъ говоритъ, что только тогда будетъ женихомъ, когда она, Одетта, явится на балъ. Несчастная дѣвушка отвѣчаетъ, что она безсильна явиться туда и въ то время можетъ только въ видѣ лебедя летать около замка. Принцъ клянется, что никогда не измѣнитъ ей. Одетта, тронутая любовью юноши, принимаетъ его клятву, но предостерегаетъ, что злой геній сдѣлаетъ все, чтобы вызвать у него клятву другой дѣвушкѣ. Зигфридъ еще разъ обѣщаетъ, что никакія чары не отнимутъ у него Одетты. Занимается заря. Одетта прощается со своимъ возлюбленнымъ и вмѣстѣ съ подругами скрывается въ развалинахъ. Свѣтъ зари становится все ярче и ярче. На озерѣ опять выплываетъ стадо лебедей, а надъ ними, тяжело махая крыльями, летитъ большой филинъ.
review_1894-95_SP_ballet_p016__b001.en: and to free Odette. She replies that this is impossible: the evil genius’s destruction will occur only at the moment when some madman sacrifices himself for love of Odette. Siegfried is ready even for this—he would gladly perish for her sake. Odette believes in his love and believes she is his first love. But tomorrow will be the day when a whole host of beauties appears at his mother’s court, and he will be obliged to choose one of them as his bride. Siegfried declares that he will become a bridegroom only when she, Odette, appears at the ball. The unhappy girl replies that she is powerless to appear there and can, at that time, fly only in the form of a swan around the castle. The Prince swears that he will never betray her. Odette, moved by the youth’s love, accepts his oath but warns him that the evil genius will do everything possible to induce him to swear an oath to another girl. Siegfried again promises that no enchantments will deprive him of Odette. Dawn breaks. Odette bids farewell to her beloved and, together with her companions, disappears into the ruins. The light of dawn grows ever brighter and brighter. Once again, a flock of swans emerges upon the lake, and above them, heavily flapping its wings, flies a large owl.

His terrible enchantment will last until someone loves her faithfully for life; only a man who has sworn love to no other girl can be her savior and restore her former appearance. Siegfried, enchanted, listens to Odette. At this moment the owl arrives, transforming into an evil genius and appearing among the ruins; he eavesdrops on their conversation and then vanishes. Siegfried is seized with horror at the thought that he might have killed Odette when she was in the form of a swan; he breaks his bow and throws it away in disgust. Odette comforts the young prince, summons all her companions, and together with them tries to distract him with dancing. review_1895-96_MSK_ballet_p013__b002.ru: На время празднествъ по случаю Священнаго Коронованія Ихъ Императорскихъ Величествъ въ Москву была перевезена С.-Петербургская балетная труппа, почти въ полномъ своемъ составѣ, во главѣ съ балеринами г-жею Леньяни и г-жею Кшесинской 2-й. Такимъ образомъ, балетные спектакли за этотъ періодъ времени давались при участіи то той, то другой труппы. Въ репертуаръ С.-Петербургской труппы были включены слѣдующіе балеты: «Лебединое озеро» (былъ исполненъ 5-го, 9-го и 21-го мая), «Привалъ кавалеріи» (26-го апрѣля и 7-го мая) и «Пробужденіе Флоры» (3-го и 23-го мая), которые шли здѣсь совершенно въ томъ же составѣ исполнителей ролей и танцевъ, какъ они обыкновенно даются на С.-Петербургской Маріинской сценѣ.
review_1895-96_MSK_ballet_p013__b002.en: For the festivities commemorating the Sacred Coronation of Their Imperial Majesties, the St. Petersburg ballet troupe was transferred to Moscow in nearly its entirety, headed by the ballerinas Mme Lennyani and Mme Kshesinskaya 2nd. Thus, ballet performances during this period were given with the participation either of one or the other troupe. The following ballets were included in the repertoire of the St. Petersburg troupe: “Swan Lake” (performed on 5th, 9th, and 21st May), “Cavalry Encampment” (26th April and 7th May), and “The Awakening of Flora” (3rd and 23rd May); these were staged here with precisely the same cast of performers and dancers as they are ordinarily presented on the St. Petersburg Mariinsky stage.

The plot is drawn from the fairy tales of A. S. Pushkin and the Brothers Grimm. The libretto was composed by H.I.H. soloist M. I. Petin and G***, music by A. N. Koreshchenko. The scenes and dances for the Moscow stage were composed and staged by A. A. Gorsky, ballet master of the Imperial Theatres of Moscow. Decorations by artist A. Ya. Golovin: Act I, Scene 1—“Garden in front of the palace”; Act II, Scene 2—“Park”; Scene 3—“Dense forest”; Scene 4—“Dwarfs’ dwelling”; Act III, Scene 5—“Forest”; Scene 6—“Rocky terrain”; Act IV, Scene 7—“Hall in the palace.” Costumes: women’s costumes by Mme Ivashchenko; men’s costumes by MM. Kaffi, Nemensky, and Pipar; footwear by Mme Levshstedt; wigs by Mr. Pedder; headgear: women’s by Mme Termen, men’s by Mr. Bruno; metallic accessories by Mr. Polyakov.

Любясь башмачкомъ, принцъ приказывается объявить по всей странѣ, что онъ избираетъ себя въ невѣсты ту, которой башмачекъ придется по ногѣ. Придворные спѣшать исполнить повелѣніе принца.

The clock strikes midnight. Cinderella, enchanted by the prince’s attention, only then recalls the promise she gave her fairy godmother and hastily departs from the ball unnoticed by those around her, as her rich attire instantly transforms into simple clothing (“Fuite de Cendrillon”—Mme Lényani and all participants). Noticing the stranger’s disappearance, Prince Charmant orders his chamberlain to pursue her, but at that moment a page enters and brings the prince the slipper lost by the princess. Enamoured of the slipper, the prince commands that it be proclaimed throughout the land that he will choose as his bride the maiden whose foot fits the slipper. The courtiers hasten to carry out the prince’s order.

The prompter announces the king’s entrance; courtiers hasten to take their places, and the royal couple, accompanied by Prince Charmant, enters the hall and takes their seats upon the throne (“Entrée du roi et de la reine”). The guests, including the Pignarol family, greet the king, who, delighted by the charm of Aloïsa and Odette, invites them to sit beside the throne. Herald trumpets announce the arrival of the embassies of Moscow and Poland (“Réception des ambassadeurs”)—MM. Lukyanov.

Входитъ Сандрильона, привѣтствуемая принцемъ Шарманомъ, который, предложивъ ей руку, представляетъ ее королю, королевѣ и всему двору («Apparition de Cendrillon»). Окружающіе поражены красотой и блестящимъ туалетомъ неизвѣстной принцессы, а семейство Пигнароль изумлено сходствомъ незнакомки съ оставшейся дома Сандрільоной. Принцъ обращаетъ всю свою любезность на новоприбывшую, а королевская чета приглашаетъ ее занять мѣсто около трона, что возбуждаетъ въ Алоизѣ и Одеттѣ злобу и зависть. По приказу принца, церемоніймейстеръ открываетъ балъ, начинающійся танцами русскихъ гостей («Danse russe»—г-жи Петипа 2-я, Легатъ 1-я, Кузьмина, Вишневская 2-я, Уракова, Горшенкова, Семенова 1-я, Онѣгина 1-я и Александрова 1-я; гг. review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p010__b001.en: and Beketov; Mmes Petipa 2nd and Petipa 1st): The chamberlain, entering hastily, announces to the King the approach of an unknown Princess, accompanied by a brilliant retinue. Cinderella enters, greeted by Prince Charmant, who, offering her his arm, presents her to the King, Queen, and the entire court (“Apparition de Cendrillon”). Those present are struck by the unknown Princess’s beauty and splendid attire, while the Pignarol family is astonished by the stranger’s resemblance to Cinderella, who remained at home. The Prince directs all his attentions toward the newcomer, and the royal couple invites her to take a seat beside the throne—an act that arouses malice and envy in Aloise and Odette. At the Prince’s command, the master of ceremonies opens the ball, which begins with dances by the Russian guests (“Danse russe”—Mmes Petipa 2nd, Legat 1st, Kuzmina, Vishnevskaya 2nd, Urakova, Gorshenkova, Semenova 1st, Onegina 1st, and Aleksandrova 1st; MM. Then, discarding this unattainable dream, Cinderella begins to blow on the fire in the hearth, which had gone out; a multitude of lively sparks flies out of the fireplace. The sparks surround the astonished girl, whirling and sparkling in an animated dance (“Pas des étincelles”)—Mmes Preobrazhenskaya, Rykhlyakova 1st, Slantsova, Matveyeva 1st, Sheberg, Nikolaeva, Andreeva, Isaeva, Kasatkina, Savitskaya, Stepanova 3rd, Kunitskaya, Fedorova 3rd, Matveyeva 3rd, Matveyeva 2nd, Vasilieva, Lavrentieva, Lobanova, Rykhlyakova 2nd, Vertinskaya, Kusterer, Golubina, Roch, Gorskaya, Ermolaeva, and Nimann. Sandrilonа appears with a bundle of firewood in her hands; her wicked sisters rush at her, shower her with reproaches, push and pinch her, and force her to finish their toilette. Ready to depart, Aloiza and Odetta dream of their triumphs at the court festival, dance, and, mocking poor Sandrilonа, compel her also to dance, ridiculing her awkwardness (“Scène dansante”). At this moment their parents enter and urge their daughters to hasten their departure for the ball. The Prince also offers Cinderella the slipper to try on; to everyone’s astonishment, the slipper itself approaches her and stops at her feet. All are struck by Cinderella’s beauty; the Prince declares his ardent love for her; her sisters beg Cinderella to forgive them for their past behaviour. The heralds proclaim Cinderella the Prince’s fiancée, to the general joy of all present. A celebration begins, consisting of various dances.

review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p007__b003.ru: бу, но съ тѣмъ, чтобы Сандрільона оставалась на балу не позже полуночи, предупреждая, что съ послѣднимъ ударомъ двѣнадцати часовъ окружающая ее роскошь исчезнетъ. По мановенію руки доброй феи, задняя стѣнка кухни исчезаетъ и открывается ночной пейзажъ съ видомъ на рѣку, посеребренную луной, и съ ярко освѣщеннымъ замкомъ, блещущимъ въ глубинѣ. Нарядные пажи и прислужницы одѣваютъ Сандрільону въ роскошные наряды, а добрая фея обучаетъ ее свѣтскимъ манерамъ и придворнымъ танцамъ («Leçon de maintien»). Сандрільонѣ подаютъ богатую карету, запряженную цугомъ, въ которой она уѣзжаетъ на праздникъ, окруженная многочисленной и блестящей свитой («Cortège et départ de Cendrillon pour le bal»).
review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p007__b003.en: but stipulating that Cinderella remain at the ball no later than midnight, warning her that with the final stroke of twelve o’clock the luxury surrounding her will vanish. At the good fairy’s wave of her hand, the rear wall of the kitchen disappears, revealing a nocturnal landscape with a moon-silvered river and a brilliantly illuminated castle gleaming in the distance. Dressed-up pages and maids dress Cinderella in luxurious attire, and the good fairy instructs her in courtly manners and court dances (“Leçon de maintien”). A rich coach, drawn by a team of horses, is brought to Cinderella, and she departs for the ball surrounded by a numerous and brilliant retinue (“Cortège et départ de Cendrillon pour le bal”).

review_1893-94_SP_ballet_p012__b001.en: The third act takes place in the garden of Prince Charmant’s palace—the décor by Academician M. I. Bocharov. The next day after the ball, Cinderella, wishing to see the Prince once more and to find the slipper she lost, appears in the avenues of the royal garden. Hearing footsteps and not knowing what to do, she falls to her knees in despair, imploring her fairy godmother to come to her aid. In response to her call, the good fairy appears, and Cinderella begs her to forgive her for returning late from the ball and to help her see the Prince once again, who is holding a festival, in the hope of finding among the guests the owner of the lost slipper (“Scène mimique de Cendrillon et de la fée bienfaisante”). The fairy agrees to grant her request and departs from the garden together with her. The King enters with the Queen and the Prince, accompanied by the guests invited to the festival. review_1895-96_SP_ballet_p024__b001.ru: настроеніе Маріи нарушается появленіемъ уланскаго корнета, который, увидя хорошенькую крестьянку, начинаетъ за ней ухаживать и сильно надоѣдаетъ ей своими назойливыми любезностями. Пьеръ, въ испугѣ, прячется за Марію... Входитъ гусарскій ротмистръ; пораженный красотою Маріи, онъ, желая избавиться отъ соперника, отдаетъ корнету приказаніе по службѣ, и тотъ, проклиная ротмистра, волей-неволей принужденъ уйти. Между тѣмъ, Пьеру удается незамѣтно скрыться, и онъ спѣшитъ въ поле предупредить крестьянъ о приходѣ солдатъ... Ухаживанье ротмистра также продолжается недолго: къ вящей его досадѣ, входитъ старый полковникъ и даетъ ему служебное порученіе, которое заставляетъ его удалиться. Полковникъ, оставшись наединѣ съ молодой дѣвушкой, любуется ея миловидностью и, въ свою очередь, осыпаетъ ее всевозможными любезностями. Марія, намѣреваясь подтрунить и вскружить голову старику, неистово кокетничаетъ съ нимъ. Очарованный полковникъ, не долго думая, обнимаетъ и цѣлуетъ ее безъ церемоніи (Scène et danse de coquetterie—г-жа Петипа 1-я и гг. Гердтъ, Легатъ 2-й, Бекефи и Лукьяновъ). review_1895-96_SP_ballet_p024__b001.en: Maria’s mood is disturbed by the appearance of a Uhlan cornet, who, upon seeing the pretty peasant girl, begins to court her and greatly annoys her with his persistent attentions. In fright, Pierre hides behind Maria… A Hussar rotmister enters; struck by Maria’s beauty, he, wishing to rid himself of a rival, gives the cornet an official order, whereupon the latter, cursing the rotmister, is reluctantly forced to depart. Meanwhile, Pierre manages to slip away unnoticed and hurries into the field to warn the peasants of the soldiers’ approach… The rotmister’s courtship also proves short-lived: to his great annoyance, an elderly colonel enters and assigns him an official errand, compelling him to withdraw. Left alone with the young girl, the colonel admires her charm and, in turn, showers her with every kind of gallantry. Maria, intending to tease and bewitch the old man, coquets with him wildly. The enchanted colonel, without hesitation, embraces and kisses her unceremoniously (Scène et danse de coquetterie—Mme Petipa 1st and MM. Gerdt, Legat 2nd, Bekefi and Lyukyanov). This scene is witnessed by the returning peasant women, who begin congratulating their friend on her success; returning…

review_1895-96_SP_ballet_p022__b005.ru: Площадь въ австрійской деревнѣ. Старшина напоминаетъ собравшимся крестьянамъ, которые оживленно бесѣдуютъ, что имъ пора отправляться въ поле на работу. Въ это время дочь старшины, Марія, тайкомъ упрашиваетъ Пьеръ придти къ ней на свиданіе и дарить ему голубую ленту. Съ нимъ условливается о свиданіи также и другая крестьянка, Тереза, причемъ также дарить ему ленту, краснаго цвѣта... Между тѣмъ, крестьяне отправляются въ поле, а крестьянки расходятся по домамъ. Пьеръ дѣлаетъ нѣсколько шаговъ, какъ бы слѣдуя за крестьянами, но самъ, отставъ отъ нихъ, незамѣтно возвращается обратно для условленнаго свиданія. Оставшись одинъ, онъ любуется подаренными ему лентами и загадываетъ, которая изъ двухъ дѣвушекъ явится первой на свиданіе и какой цвѣтъ ленты принесетъ ему больше счастья; онъ самъ находится въ нерѣшительности—которой изъ дѣвушекъ отдать предпочтеніе. review_1895-96_SP_ballet_p022__b005.en: A square in an Austrian village. The village elder reminds the assembled peasants, who are engaged in animated conversation, that it is time for them to go out to work in the fields. At this moment, the elder’s daughter, Mariya, secretly entreats Pierre to come to her for a rendezvous and presents him with a blue ribbon. Another peasant girl, Teresa, also makes an appointment with him for the same rendezvous, presenting him likewise with a red ribbon… Meanwhile, the peasants depart for the fields, and the peasant girls disperse to their homes. Pierre takes several steps, as if following the peasants, but then, falling behind them, he secretly returns unnoticed to keep the arranged rendezvous. Left alone, he admires the ribbons presented to him and wonders which of the two girls will arrive first for the rendezvous and which ribbon’s color will bring him greater happiness; he himself remains undecided—whom of the two girls to prefer.
